title: Observation of Crystallization Process in Fe-base Amorphous via 5D-STEM
content: Soft magnetic materials are used in devices such as motors and transformers that require rapid magnetization reversal, taking advantage of their ability to easily alter magnetization. To further enhance these materials, there is demand for materials with lower coercivity. Focusing on the property that smaller grain sizes yield lower coercivity, nanocrystalline soft magnetic materials have been developed. One example is FINEMET (and similarly NANOMET), which is produced by heat-treating an Fe-based amorphous alloy, resulting in the dispersion of α-Fe nanocrystals (with diameters of a few tens of nanometers) throughout the amorphous matrix. In FINEMET, a small amount of Cu is added to promote this nano-crystallization. Previous research using 3D atom probe analysis revealed that the added Cu forms clusters that serve as nucleation sites for α-Fe crystallization [1]. However, the exact atomic motion and the existence of a precursor of crystallization near the crystallization temperature have not yet been fully elucidated. Therefore, in this study, we used a five-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (5D-STEM; schematic is shown in Fig. 1.) [2], which enables the measurement of spatiotemporal distributions of diffraction patterns, to investigate the crystallization process.
